segments.say: Raw: folded chains in clear runny white. Raw egg white is clear and runny, spreading loosely in the pan, and inside it each protein chain is folded into a tight coil. Point at the folded chains on your student notes diagram before any heat is applied.
questions: What does the raw white look like, and what shape is each protein chain in?
Why does the raw white spread and run instead of holding a shape?

segments.say: Gentle heat: the folded chains unfold. The pan warms gently from below, and the heat gives the folded chains energy to open out, so each tight coil unfolds into a long loose chain. Now try the unfolding questions on your worksheet.
questions: What change in the chains tells you denaturation has started?
Has the white set yet at this stage, and how do you know?

segments.say: Bonding: chains net together, trap water. The unfolded chains link to each other with new bonds, the bonds build a network, and the water is trapped in the pockets of the network as the white turns opaque. Check the bonding stage against your student notes before moving on.
questions: What new structure do the unfolded chains build?
Where is the water once the network has formed?

segments.say: Set: firm white, water still trapped. The white is fully set - opaque, firm, and holding its shape out of the pan - and the water is still trapped inside its network. Keep the folded, unfolding, bonding, set order as you check your student notes and finish the exit ticket.
questions: Why does the set white hold its shape when it is lifted out?
What are the four stages of the change, in order?
segments.watchFor: The white sets because the heat dries the water out of it. Listen for students who explain setting as water leaving the white. Send them back to scene 3 and the network forming: The water stays trapped in the protein network - heat unfolds the chains and they bond and set. Gentle heat unfolds the folded protein chains in the egg white, the unfolded chains bond to each other and form a network that traps the water inside it, and the white turns opaque and sets firm with its water still held in the network.
